title: Pāʻia 40-acre housing project rezoning
summary: On September 8, the Maui Planning Commission voted 5 to 3 to recommend that the County Council approve the zoning change for the Pāʻia project with conditions, and unanimously backed the community plan amendment. The council will now review these recommendations. The plan covers about 40 acres and 170 homes, with at least 34 workforce rentals kept affordable forever.

timeline.text: Motion to recommend approval of the change in zoning with the council's three conditions, the owner's build order (infrastructure, parking lot, then workforce and gap-group housing) and added gap-group housing, as amended: The commission voted to recommend that the council approve the change in zoning with conditions, as amended.
The owner's representative said the project must show its water source at subdivision or it won't be approved.
Comment requesting additional affordable housing: A proposed comment asking the council to request more affordable housing was not added.

Amendment: owner to commit to meaningful additional community engagement in Pahia: Commissioners added a request that the property owner commit to meaningful, additional community engagement in Pahia.
Amendment: free parking for Maui residents at the proposed public parking lot: Commissioners added to the main motion that Maui residents can park free in the planned public parking lot.
Motion to recommend denial of the proposed change in zoning: A motion to recommend that the council deny the change in zoning failed.
The planning department, which first recommended deferral, said it could now recommend zoning approval.

Recommendation on the Pahia–Haʻikū community plan amendment from open space, agriculture and heavy industrial to public/quasi-public, multifamily, business commercial and single family: Commissioners voted unanimously to recommend that the County Council approve the community plan amendment.
The project may return to the commission later for an Special Management Area (SMA) (coastal area) permit.
The commission's attorney advised the council to hold the zoning until the state Land Use Commission approves a change from agriculture to urban.
The County Council will review the commission's recommendations.
A Pahia homeowner of 25 years testified in opposition.
A small business owner who works in Pahia testified in strong support.
The landowner's team plans two private wells for drinking water because the county system is basically at capacity.
Non-drinking water would come from an existing brackish well and treated wastewater.
The projected drinking water demand is 75,738 gallons per day.
At least 34 workforce rentals would stay affordable forever for households earning up to 120% of the area median income.
The landowner's team described about 170 homes: 120 single-family and 50 multifamily.
The landowner said the plan targets people priced out, including a 'gap group' that earns too much for traditional affordable housing but can't afford today's market.
The commission was asked only for a recommendation to the council, not a final approval.
The main item was a County Council proposal to change the community plan and zoning (land-use rules) for 40.392 acres in Pahia.
